aspects.fertilizer:
**Cotton Intercropping:**
Standing cotton must be weed-free for intercropping Canola or Raya.
Use a seed rate of 3 kg per acre.
In October, irrigate the cotton field until water reaches the top of the ridges.
After water settles, apply Canola or Raya seed using a double broadcast method.
Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation.
Cut cotton sticks slightly high after the cotton harvest ends.

**General Fertilizer Management:**
Use balanced fertilizer to counter adverse climate change impacts and improve yield.
Determine per-acre fertilizer rates based on laboratory soil tests.
Apply recommended rates on average fertility soils.
For private company seeds, follow their recommended application rates.

**Cholistan Raya, Super Raya, AARI Canola, Sarson DGL, and Canzola:**
Apply 35 kg Nitrogen, 30 kg Phosphorus, and 12 kg Potash per acre.
Option 1 at sowing is 1.25 bags DAP and 0.5 bag SOP.
Option 2 at sowing is 3.25 bags SSP 18 percent, 0.5 bag Urea, and 0.5 bag SOP.
Option 3 at sowing is 1 bag Nitrophos, 2.25 bags SSP 18 percent, and 0.5 bag SOP.

**TM Canola, Rachna Canola, Sandal Canola, Khanpur Canola, Barani Canola, Super Canola, and Other Recommended Varieties:**
Apply 35 kg Nitrogen, 35 kg Phosphorus, and 25 kg Potash per acre.
Option 1 at sowing is 1.5 bags DAP and 1 bag SOP.
Option 2 at sowing is 4 bags SSP 18 percent, 0.5 bag Urea, and 1 bag SOP.
Option 3 at sowing is 1 bag Nitrophos, 2.75 bags SSP 18 percent, and 0.5 bag SOP.

**Rain-fed (Barani) Areas:**
Apply the entire quantity of fertilizer at sowing time.

**Irrigated Areas:**
Apply all phosphorus and potash plus one-third of nitrogen at sowing time.
Apply the remaining nitrogen in two equal splits: half with the first irrigation and half before flowering.

**Secondary Nutrients and Micronutrients:**
Apply 4 to 5 kg sulfur per acre with the second irrigation to improve yield and quality.
Use Ammonium Sulphate instead of Urea if available.
Apply Boron to improve flowering and pollination.
If SOP is unavailable, use MOP combined with 2 kg sulfur per acre.

**Punjab Advisory and Soil Testing:**
Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore developed the free Khad Hisab mobile app on Google Play Store.
The app calculates balanced fertilizer doses with or without a soil test report.
Farmers can watch the introductory video inside the app for usage instructions.
Contact the nearest government soil and water testing laboratory for more information.
aspects.harvesting:
Northern Punjab:
AARI Canola is sown from September 1 to September 15 and harvested from February 1 to mid-February. TM Canola, Rachna Canola, Khanpur Canola, Barani Canola, Super Canola, Sandal Canola, and other approved varieties are sown from September 20 to October 20 and harvested in March.

Central and Southern Punjab:
AARI Canola is sown from September 1 to September 30 and harvested from mid-January to mid-February. TM Canola, Rachna Canola, Khanpur Canola, Barani Canola, Super Canola, Sandal Canola, and other approved varieties are sown from October 1 to October 31 and harvested in March.

Approved Varieties and Soil:
Loam or light loam soil is suitable for approved canola varieties. Canola harvesting takes place between March 1 and mid-April.

Cotton Intercropping:
Cotton fields must be weed-free before intercropping with canola or raya. Use a seed rate of 3 kilograms per acre. Irrigate the cotton field in October so water rises over the ridges. Double broadcast seed after water settles. Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation. Cut cotton sticks slightly high after cotton harvest ends.

Harvesting Signs:
Harvesting early causes weak seeds and lower oil content. Harvesting late causes pods to burst, seeds to shed, and yield loss. Harvest when leaves turn yellow, grains turn reddish, and 70 percent of pods turn brown in canola or sarson, or 80 percent in raya.

Post-Harvest and Threshing:
Place harvested crop on a raised spot to avoid rain damage. Sun-dry the crop for 6 to 10 days before threshing. Threshers are available for seed separation.

Combine Harvesting:
Combine harvesters are recommended for large cultivated areas. Harvest when 90 percent or more pods turn brown. Change the combine harvester screen and make proper adjustments. Maintain a plant population of 90,000 plants per acre for combine harvesting.

Storage:
Ensure seed moisture is 8 percent or less and seeds crack when chewed. High moisture causes fungus. Keep varieties separate during storage. Inspect warehouses regularly for insect attacks. Fumigate storage facilities with 30 to 35 tablets of Aluminium Phosphide per 1,000 cubic feet.

Pesticide Application:
Use a flat fan or floodjet nozzle for weed control. Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect control. Bury empty chemical bottles in the ground and dispose of cardboard boxes.

Domestic Oil Refining:
Extract raw oil using a kohlu or expeller. Heat 5 kilograms of raw canola oil to 85 degrees Celsius without boiling. Add 150 grams of finely ground gachni or Fuller's earth. Stir well with a spoon for 5 minutes and remove from heat. Hang a triangular thick cloth bag from a sturdy stand or charpai over a clean pot. Filter the lukewarm oil through the bag.
aspects.irrigation:
Sowing and pre-irrigation:
Under unavoidable circumstances, sow canola in dry land, make ridges, and then apply water.
In salt-affected soil, sowing can be done by broadcasting in standing mud like berseem.
Apply two pre-sowing irrigations before sowing if broadcasting in moist soil.

Intercropping in standing cotton:
Ensure the cotton crop is free of weeds for mixed cultivation of canola or raya.
Use a seed rate of 3 kg per acre.
Irrigate the cotton field in October so water rises over the ridges.
Double broadcast canola or raya seed after the water settles down.
Apply recommended fertilizer with the first irrigation.
Cut cotton sticks slightly high when the cotton crop ends.

Irrigation schedule:
Three to four irrigations are sufficient for canola, raya, and sarson.
Apply the first irrigation 25 to 30 days after germination.
Apply the second irrigation at flowering.
Apply the third irrigation in a light amount near pod formation.
Apply a light irrigation in case of severe frost.
Irrigate according to crop need when planted on ridges.

Weather and water management:
Take special care of irrigation during drought.
Plant on ridges to protect from heavy rains, minimize crop damage, and drain excess water easily.
Check the weather forecast before sowing or applying irrigation.
Sow at the recommended time and maintain plant protection.
aspects.machinery:
General Sowing:
Prepare land thoroughly and use a laser land leveler for leveling fields for canola, taramira, toria, and raya.
Sow canola, taramira, toria, and raya in good moisture (tar wattar) in rows spaced 1 to 1.5 feet apart.
Maintain a plant population of 60,000 to 70,000 plants per acre.
A small seed drill is available for sowing and gives very good results.
Do not exceed a seed depth of 1 to 1.5 inches.

Ridge Sowing:
After land preparation, broadcast seed and fertilizer, run a plow and plank, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A planter called a ridger-cum-seeder is available in the market for this method.

Rain-fed (Barani) Areas:
To conserve rainfall moisture, plow empty fields deeply before the monsoon season.
Strengthen field borders, plow as needed, level the land, and plow in the opposite direction of the slope.
Do not plow fields after the monsoon season.
Plow twice and run a plank before sowing to prevent moisture loss.
Ensure fields are leveled and weed-free at sowing time.
Prepare land during the evening or before sunrise to avoid moisture loss.

Harvesting and Threshing:
Place harvested canola and raya on elevated ground to prevent rain damage to pods.
Dry the harvested crop in the sun for 6 to 10 days before threshing to separate the seed.
Threshers are available for threshing.
Use a combine harvester if oilseed crops are grown on large acreage.
Harvest with a combine harvester only when 90 percent or more of the pods have turned brown.
Change the combine harvester sieve and make appropriate adjustments.
Maintain a plant population of 90,000 plants per acre for canola, raya, or sarson if harvesting by combine harvester.

Spraying Machinery:
Test the machine with plain water before spraying canola to determine water volume.
Use the recommended water volume to ensure uniform spray application.
Do not spray during strong winds.
Do not stand facing against the wind while spraying.
Avoid repeated use of chemicals from the same chemical group.
Use a flat fan nozzle or a flood jet nozzle for weed control.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect control.
Bury empty chemical bottles in the soil and dispose of cardboard boxes.
aspects.other:
Rain-fed areas:
Summer rains are very important for Rabi crops including canola.
Canola is planted using the moisture conserved from summer rains.
Methods should be adopted to absorb and preserve summer rainwater in the soil rather than letting it run off.
Properly conserving monsoon rainwater can increase Rabi crop yields by 20 to 25 percent.

Sag harvesting:
Plucking sag from the canola crop increases the risk of aphid attack.
Plucking sag reduces crop yield.
A separate area should be allocated for harvesting sag to protect the crop sown for seed.

High-rainfall areas:
Canola must be sown on ridges.

Climate change precautions:
Climate change causes harmful impacts on canola through drought and unexpected heavy rains.
Canola should be sown at the recommended time to protect it from climate change.
Farmers must ensure proper plant protection.
Check the weather forecast before sowing or applying water.

Farmer training:
Canola training programs are organized at the district and tehsil levels.
Agriculture experts teach modern canola cultivation technology to farmers and agriculture department extension staff.
aspects.overview:
**Punjab Statistics:**
In 2020-21, canola area was 413.50 thousand acres (167.34 thousand hectares), total production was 267.26 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 16.16 maunds per acre.
In 2021-22, canola area was 585.50 thousand acres (236.94 thousand hectares), total production was 403.00 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 17.21 maunds per acre.
In 2022-23, canola area was 1055.10 thousand acres (426.98 thousand hectares), total production was 665.71 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.77 maunds per acre.
In 2023-24, canola area was 605.20 thousand acres (244.91 thousand hectares), total production was 314.47 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 12.99 maunds per acre.
Provisional estimates for 2024-25 show canola area at 820.65 thousand acres (332.10 thousand hectares), total production at 499.94 thousand metric tons, and average yield at 15.23 maunds per acre.

**Canola Overview:**
Canola is included in the 2025-26 oilseed plan to increase domestic edible oil production and reduce import dependency.
Its oil contains very low harmful ingredients.
The crop tolerates chemical fertilizers well, resists lodging, and produces good yields.
Canola meal can be fed to milch animals and poultry.
Recommended canola varieties are TM Canola, Super Canola, Rachna Canola, Khanpur Canola, Barani Canola, and Sandal Canola.

**Canola Varieties:**
TM Canola matures in 130 to 140 days, has long pods and thick grains, contains about 42 percent oil, yields up to 30 maunds per acre, and suits cotton areas.
Super Canola resists water scarcity and lodging, has high pod counts, contains up to 43 percent oil, yields an average of 25 maunds per acre, and has 38 maunds per acre potential.
Rachna Canola resists lodging, yields well on less water, contains 40 to 42 percent oil, 9 percent Omega-3, and yields an average of 28 to 30 maunds per acre with 35 maunds potential.
Khanpur Canola tolerates water shortage and heat, contains up to 46 percent oil, yields an average of 40 maunds per acre, and has higher potential.
Barani Canola was developed by Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal, has yield potential up to 33.43 maunds per acre, contains 41.11 percent oil, and has harmful content under 1 percent.
AARI Canola is a heat-tolerant Raya variety maturing in 110 to 120 days with 38 percent oil and 12 percent Omega-3 for heart and blood pressure patients.
AARI Canola yields 18 to 20 maunds per acre with 30 maunds potential, resists pod shattering, allows sugarcane intercropping, and provides meal for milch animals and poultry.
Canzola is also a recommended Raya variety.

**Soil and Cultivation:**
Canola requires well-drained medium to heavy loam soils.
Highly saline and waterlogged soils are unsuitable.
In rice zones, clay soils, and high rainfall areas, planting on ridges saves water and protects the crop.
Adaptive Research Gujranwala trials confirm good yields when sowing canola on ridges after rice.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Seed Treatment:
Apply recommended fungicide at 1 g per 1 kg seed with strictly measured water. For stem rot prevention, treat seed with 1 g Thiophanate-methyl per 1 kg seed.

Cultural Management:
Harvesting saag increases aphid attack and lowers seed yield; reserve a separate area for saag. Complete sowing in the first week of October to prevent aphids. Avoid early sowing, practice crop rotation, eradicate weeds, and destroy crop residues. Never hoe immediately after spraying.

Termite Control:
Termites attack underground plant parts in dry weather. Flood 1 liter Fipronil 5% SC per acre with water, or apply during rauni in empty fields. For barani areas, broadcast 15 to 20 kg fine soil mixed with recommended poison before sowing and plow.

Grasshopper Control:
Risk is higher near sugarcane, maize, and sorghum. Spray 330 ml Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or 250 ml Bifenthrin 10 EC per acre.

Mustard Sawfly:
Wrinkled dark greenish-black larvae attack in October and November. Per acre spray: 80 ml Spinetoram 120 SC, 330 ml Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5% EC, 200 ml Emamectin benzoate 1.9 EC, or 30 g Fipronil 80 WG.

Painted Bug:
Nymphs and adults attack in October and November. Per acre spray: 400 ml Abamectin plus Thiamethoxam 108 SC, 100 g Dinotefuran 20% SG, 250 g Acephate 75 SP, or 250 ml Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cabbage Butterfly:
Larvae feed in patches. Per acre spray: 80 ml Chlorantraniliprole plus Thiamethoxam 300 SC, 80 ml Spinetoram 120 SC, 50 ml Flubendiamide 480 SC, or 250 ml Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC.

Aphid Control:
Attacks occur from mid-January to late March. Per acre spray: 24 g Thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 g Dinotefuran 20% SG, 60 g Flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 ml Clothianidin 20 EC.

Biological Control Punjab:
Green lacewing Chrysoperla cards control aphids. Punjab Agriculture Extension provides free cards from eleven labs: Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Layyah, Vehari, Pakpattan, Sheikhupura, Jhang, Muzaffargarh, Okara, and Toba Tek Singh.

Disease Management:
Rates are per liter of water. White rust: spray 1.25 ml Propiconazole or Difenoconazole. Epidemic blight at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius during rain: spray 1 g Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2.5 ml Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole. Downy mildew: spray 5 g Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium or 6 g Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil. Bacterial stem rot during smog: spray 2.5 ml Benzothiazolinone, 1 g Streptomycin sulfate, or 6 ml Kasugamycin. Stem rot: spray 2.5 ml Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole. Plant blight: spray 1 g Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 3.5 g Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin. Rust: spray 1 g Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2 ml Propiconazole.

Application Rules:
Spray only at economic thresholds in the evening to protect pollinators, ladybird beetles, syrphid flies, and Chrysoperla. Use hollow cone nozzles for insect pests and flat fan or flood jet nozzles for weeds. Wear goggles, gloves, and rubber boots. Bury empty pesticide bottles and destroy cardboard boxes.
aspects.sowing:
Northern Punjab:
Sow AARI Canola from September 1 to September 15, and harvest from February 1 to mid-February. Sow TM Canola, Rachna Canola, Khanpur Canola, Barani Canola, Super Canola, Sandal Canola, and other approved varieties from September 20 to October 20, and harvest in March.

Central and Southern Punjab:
Sow AARI Canola from September 1 to September 30, and harvest from mid-January to mid-February. Sow TM Canola, Rachna Canola, Khanpur Canola, Barani Canola, Super Canola, Sandal Canola, and other approved varieties from October 1 to October 31, and harvest in March.

General Canola Sowing:
Overall canola sowing occurs from October 1 to mid-November. Loam and light loam soils are suitable. Consider temperature and rainfall forecasts before sowing. Prepare land thoroughly and level it with a laser land leveler. Sow in moist soil at a row-to-row distance of 1 to 1.5 feet. Maintain 60,000 to 70,000 plants per acre. Seed depth must not exceed 1 to 1.5 inches. Small seed drills give good results. In unavoidable situations, sow in dry soil, make ridges, and then apply water. In salt-affected soil, broadcast seed into standing water like berseem. If broadcasting in moist soil, perform two pre-soaking irrigations before sowing.

Ridge Sowing in Heavy Soil, High Rainfall, and Rice Areas:
Ridge sowing saves water, protects crops from excess rain, and delivers good yields after rice harvest based on experiments at Adaptive Research Gujranwala. Broadcast seed and fertilizer, plow and plank, then make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor or an available ridger-cum-seeder planter.

Sugarcane Intercropping:
Intercrop short-duration varieties UAF-11, AARI Canola, and TM Canola in September-sown sugarcane. Use 1 kg seed per acre. Sow 1 canola line between sugarcane rows spaced 2.5 feet apart, or 2 lines if rows are 4 feet apart. This provides extra yield and protects sugarcane from frost.

Cotton Intercropping:
Intercrop in weed-free standing cotton during October using 3 kg seed per acre. Irrigate until water reaches ridge tops. After water settles, double broadcast the seed. Apply recommended fertilizer with the first water. Cut cotton sticks slightly high after harvest.

Rain-fed Areas:
Conserving monsoon rainwater increases rabi yields by 20 to 25 percent. Before monsoon, plow deeply, strengthen field bunds, level land, and plow across slopes. Do not plow after the rainy season. Before sowing, plow and plank twice to conserve moisture. Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise.

Thinning:
Thin before the first irrigation when plants have 4 leaves. Remove weak and diseased plants. Keep plant-to-plant distance at 9 to 12 inches.

Weed Control:
In moderate weather at 35 degrees Celsius or below, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing. If drill sowing in moist soil, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre before the last plowing. For ridge sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre within 24 hours of sowing.
aspects.varieties:
Canola Varieties:
Canola oil has low harmful components and is suitable for eating.
The crop tolerates chemical fertilizers well, has low lodging risk, and produces high yields.
Canola meal can be fed to milch animals and poultry.
Recommended varieties include TM Canola, Super Canola, Rachna Canola, Khanpur Canola, Barani Canola, Sandal Canola, UAF-11, AARI Canola, Canzola, Barani Star, and Cholistan Star.
Barani Canola from BARI Chakwal yields up to 33.43 maunds per acre, contains up to 41.11 percent oil, and has less than 1 percent harmful content.
Sandal Canola has long pods, thick black seeds, over 42 percent oil, and yields 25 to 30 maunds per acre or more.
Heat-tolerant varieties include Chakwal Raya, Khanpur Raya, Super Raya, AARI Canola, Cholistan Raya, and Canzola.

Punjab Sowing and Soil:
Northern Punjab sowing time is 20 September to 20 October.
Central and Southern Punjab sowing time is 1 to 31 October.
Harvesting takes place in March.
Loam or light loam soil is most suitable.
Prepare land well, level with a laser leveler, and plant seed at a maximum depth of 1.5 inches.

Seed Rates and Sources:
Certified seed is available in limited quantities from Punjab Seed Corporation, NARC Islamabad, AARI Faisalabad Oilseeds Department, Khanpur Oilseeds Research Station, RARI Bahawalpur, BARI Chakwal, and registered private companies.
Always use Federal Seed Certification Department certified seed with at least 80 percent germination under good moisture conditions.
Irrigated areas require 1.5 to 2 kg seed per acre.
Barani areas require 1.5 to 2.5 kg seed per acre.
Cholistan requires 3 to 4 kg seed per acre.

Intercropping:
In September sugarcane, intercrop short-duration varieties UAF-11, AARI Canola, or TM Canola at 1 kg seed per acre.
Plant 1 row of Canola between 2.5-foot sugarcane rows, or 2 rows between 4-foot sugarcane rows.
In weed-free standing cotton, flood over ridges in October and double broadcast Canola at 3 kg seed per acre after water settles.
Apply fertilizer with first irrigation and cut cotton stalks high after harvest.

Fertilizer per Acre:
Nutrient requirements are 35 kg nitrogen, 35 kg phosphorus, and 25 kg potash.
Apply 1.5 bags DAP and 1 bag SOP at sowing.
Alternatively, use 4 bags SSP 18 percent, 0.5 bag Urea, and 1 bag SOP.
Another alternative is 1 bag Nitrophos, 2.75 bags SSP 18 percent, and 0.5 bag SOP.

Disease Management:
Treat seed with recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kg seed.
For stem rot, treat seed with Thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kg seed, or spray Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter water.
For epidemic blight during rain at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius, spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter.
For downy mildew, spray Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams per liter or Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter.
For plant blight, spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter or Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter.
Control wilt and blights by rotating crops, destroying debris, and avoiding early sowing.
aspects.weeds:
Common Weeds:
Canola fields commonly have wild oat, canary grass (dumbi sitti), lashkni booti, bathu, karund, shahtra, and it-sit.

Cultural and Non-Chemical Control:
The dab method is highly suitable for non-chemical weed control.
After soaking irrigation or rainfall when soil is in workable moisture condition, plough the field and apply a heavy planking.
Leave the field for 5 to 7 days so weeds emerge.
These weeds are destroyed during final seedbed preparation.
Perform dry hoeing after crop emergence, preferably before rain.
Do the first hoeing before the first irrigation.
Do the second hoeing after irrigation when the soil reaches workable moisture condition.
Thin the crop when it develops four leaves to maintain recommended plant spacing.
To manage wilt or seedling rot, treat seed with recommended fungicides, avoid early sowing, remove weeds, and rotate crops.
Seedling rot causes rotten seeds, wilting, drying plants, and split root bark.

Pre-Emergence Chemical Control:
Spray recommended herbicide pendimethalin at 1000 ml per acre before crop emergence.
If heavy weed infestation is expected, spray recommended chemicals immediately after sowing.
In moderate weather with temperatures at 35 degrees Celsius or below, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing.
For drill and workable moisture sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final ploughing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.

Post-Emergence Chemical Control:
Spray 400 to 500 ml Metazachlor 50 percent SC per acre to control it-sit germinated within two weeks of crop emergence.
Metazachlor 50 percent SC spray can be applied without a protective shield.

Application Safety and Equipment:
Use a flat fan nozzle or flood jet nozzle for weed sprays.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect sprays.
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after spraying herbicides.
Hoeing after spray breaks the chemical barrier, allows weeds to regrow, and exposes the farmer to toxic flying chemical dust through skin and respiration.
Bury empty chemical bottles in the soil and destroy cardboard packaging.
